basics.name: Jonathon Tanks
basics.label: Materials Scientist
basics.summary: American living in Japan, trying to figure out how to make better materials by first learning how they breakdown

work.name: National Institute for Materials Science (NIMS), Polymer Matrix Composites Group
work.summary: Studying degradation and failure behavior of polymers and their composites, and using that knowledge to both recycle them more efficient and make them more robust.

volunteer.summary: Review manuscripts for various academic journals.

courses: Degradation Kinetics of Epoxy Resin in Acidic Environments

awards.summary: Full financial support (tuition + stipend) for pursuing a PhD at Tokyo Tech; selected through the Embassy Recommendation program (~10% acceptance rate)

publications.name: Room-temperature material recycling/upcycling of polyamide waste enabled by cosolvent-tunable dissolution kinetics
publications.summary: In-depth investigation into the dissolution mechanism of polyamide (nylon) plastics and how it is affected by cosolvents, and application to room-temperature material recycling.

publications.name: Durable and recyclable biomimetic glycol lignin/polyolefin compounds for a circular economy
publications.summary: Elucidation of how lignin improves the UV resistance of polyolefins by simultaneously acting as antioxidant, absorbant, and reinforcement, with application to closed-loop mechanical recycling.

publications.name: Glycol lignin/MAH-g-PP blends and composites with exceptional mechanical properties for automotive applications
publications.summary: Fabrication of polypropylene/lignin blends and their short-carbon fiber composites, exhibiting greatly enhanced mechanical properties through reinforcement around the fiber/matrix interface.
